question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Has bigger fish to fry

options.text: Has easier plans to solve the issue
Has more important work to do

solution:
The correct answer is **"Has more important work to do."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The idiom "has bigger fish to fry" means that someone has more important or pressing matters to attend to.**
 
• अधिक महत्वपूर्ण या अत्यावश्यक मामले हैं.
 
• The phrase is often used to indicate that someone doesn't have time for something less important or trivial.
 
• The idiom originated from the practice of fishermen choosing to catch larger, more valuable fish instead of smaller ones.
 
• Grammatically, "has bigger fish to fry" is in the present tense and is often used in the third person.
 
 
• Example: I do not have a lot of time to spend on this issue. I have bigger fish to fry.
 
 
 
• Thus, it is clear that option 3 correctly explains the given idiom.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.
